label: D1 after an unrewarded visit to S1 (evidence for S2 / leaning a2)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO or D2). It is strongest and most reliable when the previous trial was unrewarded and reached S1, i.e. observed evidence that S1 is bad and S2 good (dev precision 0.83, recall 0.49, mass recall 0.62). Overall it is a broader D1 feature for being unrewarded and leaning toward a2: D1 & prev_reward==0 covers 76% of activation mass but has precision 0.44. Adding the agent upcoming choice, D1 & prev_reward==0 & (prev_state==1 | action==2), gives a slightly higher F1 (0.64 vs 0.61). I recorded the simpler predicate, which uses only observed variables. Activations are higher when good==2, when the upcoming choice is a2 (91% of mass), and when value is mid-range (7.1-7.5); it is almost silent when value > 7.7 or when the policy strongly favours a1. Misses: weaker activations after rewarded trials (often at rel +1, the window last trial) and unrewarded S2 visits followed by an a2 choice. False positives: unrewarded S1 visits where the agent keeps choosing a1 (S1 still believed good).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=D1 (+5.46), phase=D1 & last=a2 S1 u (+3.83), phase=D1 & choice_bin=decile 1 (9 = most a1) (+3.67), phase=D1 & choice_bin=decile 2 (9 = most a1) (+3.16), ep_bucket=4 (+2.89), prev_state=1 (+2.86). Lower it: value_bin=decile 8 (9 = highest) (-6.25), prev_state=2 (-6.06), phase=D2 (-5.47), phase=GO (-4.68).
